comments.author: @stefanhartmann862
comments.text:
The problem with this vision is the absolute atomization of society. 
If, in the end, everyone gets exactly what they want, we lose all cultural context because we no longer have any common references.
South Park is not relevant because the episodes are entertaining and funny, but because South Park provides common cultural references.
One could even say that these shared cultural references are the foundation of every culture. 
The concept presented here is as dystopian as it gets.

comments.author: @BoidyB
comments.text:
I don't buy that you need to maintain a simulation to generate a cohesive story.

You could get an LLM today to generate a screenplay of a star trek episode. It would be shit writing, but it would have a fairly cohesive narrative arc and plausible continuity. It doesnt have a simulation of the enterprise running in order to do that, it just has a baked in understanding of narrative and continuity.
Similarly with models of the future, I don't see them needing a simulation running in order to generate an extra episode.

I get it that hes trying to invent a new medium thats kind of a hybrid MMO + episodic narrative with IP constraints. Maybe a simulation is needed for that kind of thing, but I don't think that its necessary to get your "click the plus icon in Netflix to get a new episode" dream.
